units: B. Bath. 86ᵇ שאני בהמה דסַרְכָא (Ms. R. דמְסָרְכָא Pa., v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note

senses.gloss: it is different with taking possession of an animal, because it clutches (the ground).
units: <cite ref="Chullin 51a:7">Ḥull. 51ᵃ</cite> <he>אית לה מידי למִיסְרַךְ</he> the animal has something to clutch (when falling, so as to break the shock); <he>והאי לית … למ׳</he> while this (kid) had nothing to cling to.

<cite ref="Chullin 51a:7">Ib.</cite> top <he>ליכא מידי למיסרך</he> there is no object for the blood to hang to (around which to coagulate); <he>כיון דאיכא מחט … מיסרך הוה סָרֵיךְ</he> since a needle has been found there, if the perforation had taken place before slaughtering, blood would have clung round it; a. e.—Part. pass. <cite ref="O01616"><he>סָרִיךְ</he></cite>; f. <cite ref="O01617"><he>סְרִיכָא</he></cite>; pl. <cite ref="O01632"><he>סְרִיכִין</he></cite>; <cite ref="O01617"><he>סְרִיכָן</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Gittin 68b:16">Gitt. 68ᵇ</cite> <he>שוטה בחדא מילתא לא ס׳</he> an insane person does not cling to one fiction (he will betray his insanity in some other way than merely by repeating the same thing).
<cite ref="Chullin 46b">Ḥull. 46ᵇ</cite> <he>הני … דס׳ להדדי</he> two lobes of the lungs which adhere to each other (by a membrane).
Ned. 50ᵇ ואם אית כיבא ס׳ עלה if there be a sore in the bowels, it will cling to it (v. טְרוֹמִיטָא); a. e.—2) to confound, v. infra.
<cite ref="Beitzah 11a:4">Bets. 11ᵃ</cite> <he>סָרוּכֵי סָרוּךְ וסליקו</he> they clutched and climbed up.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 20a:1">B. Kam. 20ᵃ</cite> <he>סריך סליק וכ׳</he> it climbed, came up and ate &c.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 20a:1">Ib.</cite> <he>לסרוכי ולמסלק</he> (not <he>לסרוכיה</he>; Ms. F. <he>למיסרך</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 30) to climb up; a. e.
<cite ref="Chullin 111a:10">Ḥull. 111ᵃ</cite> <he>חלב סָרוּכֵי מְסָרֵיךְ</he> (not <he>סרוכיה</he>) milk adheres (and penetrates), opp. <he>מישרק שריק</he> glides off.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 22b:9">Ab. Zar. 22ᵇ</cite> <he>מְסָרֵיךְ אבתרה</he> (Ms. M. <he>מִיסְרַךְ סָרֵיךְ</he>) he clings to her (runs after her).

<cite ref="Pesachim 51a:1">Pes. 51ᵃ</cite> <he>משום דמְסָרְכֵי מילתא</he> (Ms. M. <he>דסריכי</he>; Ms. O. <he>דמְסָרְבֵי מילתא במילתא</he>, v. <cite ref="O01513"><he>סְרַב</he> II</cite>) because they confound one thing with another (if you permit them one thing, they will allow themselves another); <he>הנך אינשי נמי סַרְכֵי מילתא</he> (Ms. M. <he>סְרִיכֵי</he>, Ms. O. <he>מסרבי מילתא במילתא</he>) those people (ignorant Jews) will likewise confound &c.; a. e.

senses.gloss: to cling to. Ab. Zar. l. c. כרון דמִיסְּרִיךְ Rashi (ed. דמיגרי), v. גְּרֵי.
